tasks.prompt: After lining a root filled clay sewer in a western Canadian city, one home on the reach still backs up in dry weather.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian home backup after lining. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Main CCTV after lining shows a smooth, sealed pipe with no roots.
All other homes on the reach drain normally after lining.
A lateral camera finds roots entering at the lateral connection where the liner was cut open.
The lateral itself beyond the connection is sound on camera.
Dye from the home is delayed at the connection and then flows freely.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The liner has failed along the whole reach
The home plumbing is blocked inside the house
Roots are growing through the liner wall along the main
Roots are re-entering at the reopened lateral connection, the one unsealed opening left in the lined main

inference.explanation: The lined main is sealed and neighbours are fine, the lateral beyond the connection is sound, and roots sit exactly at the reopened cut. That isolates the connection opening as the entry point.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best supports a connection seal repair?

options.label: A whole reach liner thickness test
Connection camera log showing root entry at the cut edge, with the liner and lateral otherwise sound
A home plumbing inspection report

nextClue.explanation: The connection log shows the only opening where roots enter, which is what a connection seal must close.

clueText.nc-a: Thickness testing does not locate an entry point at a connection.
clueText.nc-b: The log shows roots at the cut edge only, with smooth liner upstream and downstream.
clueText.nc-c: The home plumbing was not inspected, and dye delay sits at the connection, not inside the house.

tasks.prompt: A lift station in a prairie town trips its lead pump twice a week, and each time the crew pulls a fibrous ball off the impeller.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian lift station pump ragging. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The material pulled off is woven synthetic fibre that does not tear like toilet paper.
Toilet paper samples from the wet well break apart in water within minutes, and the fibre ball does not.
The catchment includes an apartment block where wipes are found in the garbage room bins.
Grease levels in the wet well are low and the floats are clean.
After a wipe education notice to the block, trips fall for one month, then return.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Non dispersible wipes are reaching the pump and ragging the impeller
Grease is building up and stalling the pump
The impeller is worn out and catching ordinary toilet paper
Roots are entering the wet well and wrapping the pump

inference.explanation: The fibre is synthetic and does not disperse, grease is low, and trips track wipe use at the apartment block. A worn impeller would catch paper too, but paper breaks down and is not what is recovered.

nextClue.prompt: Which sample check best confirms the material for the education follow up?

options.label: Grease depth log for the wet well
Pump age and impeller wear measurement
Dispersibility test and fibre identification on recovered material, logged with photos from each trip event

nextClue.explanation: Identifying the recovered material as non dispersible wipe fibre is the direct proof behind the trips.

clueText.nc-a: Grease depths are already low, so a grease log does not explain fibre on the impeller.
clueText.nc-b: Wear measurements describe the pump, not the material wrapped around it.
clueText.nc-c: Recovered balls test as synthetic wipe fibre that stays intact after an hour in water.

tasks.prompt: A gravity sewer in a coastal British Columbia town blocks at the same bend every few weeks with a mat of intact sheet material.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian gravity sewer blocking at a bend. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Jetting returns contain whole sheets labelled by residents as flushable wipes, still intact.
The mat forms at a bend where a lateral enters at a sharp angle.
Upstream straight reaches on CCTV are clean.
No roots or grease are seen at the bend on CCTV.
Toilet paper is never found intact in the returns.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Toilet paper is matting at the bend like the wipes
Wipes are surviving the trip through the sewer and matting at the bend and lateral entry
Grease is gluing ordinary paper into a mat at the bend
The bend has collapsed and is catching all solids

inference.explanation: Intact wipes in returns, a clean upstream pipe, and no grease or roots isolate wipes catching at a flow disturbance. Paper disperses, and a collapse would show on camera and catch everything, not just sheets.

nextClue.prompt: Which comparison best confirms wipes as the mat material?

options.label: Side by side soak test of recovered sheets and toilet paper, with the recovered sheets staying whole
A bend angle survey of the reach
A grease sample from the downstream manhole

nextClue.explanation: The soak test separates material that disperses from material that survives to form mats.

clueText.nc-a: Recovered sheets stay whole after soaking while toilet paper falls apart in minutes.
clueText.nc-b: The bend angle explains where mats catch, not what the mats are made of.
clueText.nc-c: No grease was seen at the bend, so a grease sample does not explain the sheets.

tasks.prompt: A sewer below an active construction site in Alberta blocks twice in one month with gravel and chunks of concrete in the returns.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian sewer below a construction site. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Jetting returns contain angular gravel and grey concrete chunks up to 40 mm.
CCTV shows a pile of coarse debris resting in the pipe below an open cut crossing.
Upstream of the site the pipe is clean and homes report no problems.
The site has an open trench over the sewer and no cover on an exposed manhole for several days.
Debris size matches the granular bedding used on the site.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Road gravel is washing in through home laterals all over the catchment
The pipe bedding is entering through a broken wall along the whole reach
Construction debris entered the sewer at the site and settled in the pipe below it
Residents are dumping renovation waste into their toilets

inference.explanation: Debris sits below the site, matches site bedding, the upstream pipe is clean, and a manhole stood open at the trench. A broken wall would show on camera and catchment wide sources would not concentrate below one site.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best ties the debris to the site for the cleanup claim?

options.label: Home renovation permits for the catchment
Dated photos of the open manhole and trench plus a debris sample matched to site bedding material
A full catchment CCTV survey

nextClue.explanation: Dated site photos with a matched material sample directly link entry point and material.

clueText.nc-a: Permits do not show debris entering this sewer at this site.
clueText.nc-b: Photos show the uncovered manhole at the trench and the sample matches the site bedding gradation.
clueText.nc-c: A catchment survey is wider than needed when the pile already sits below one open site.

tasks.prompt: A flat sewer reach in a Manitoba town keeps collecting sand and grit even though it is jetted on schedule.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian flat reach with grit accumulation. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: CCTV shows a shallow sag in the middle of the reach holding standing water.
Grit collects in the sag and the pipe is clean on both sides of it.
Flow velocity measured in the sag is well below the rest of the reach.
Upstream catch basins and streets drain to this reach after spring melt.
Jetting moves the grit a short distance and it resettles in the sag within weeks.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The jetting crew is using too little water on every reach in town
Homes are discharging sand from water softeners
The pipe is leaking grit in through its joints along the whole reach
The sag drops velocity so grit carried in melt water settles there and stays

inference.explanation: Grit sits only in the sag, velocity there is lowest, and the rest of the reach and other town reaches stay clean under the same crew. Joint leakage would show grit at joints, not one mid reach pile.

nextClue.prompt: Which measurement best confirms the sag as the settling cause?

options.label: Water softener count for homes on the reach
Jetting water volume records for the town
Level survey through the reach paired with CCTV showing the grit pile inside the surveyed sag limits

nextClue.explanation: Tying the pile location to surveyed sag limits proves the low spot is where material drops out.

clueText.nc-a: Softener discharge is water, not the coarse grit found in the pile.
clueText.nc-b: The same crew and volumes keep other reaches clean, so volume alone does not explain one sag pile.
clueText.nc-c: The survey shows a 12 m sag and the grit pile sits entirely within those 12 m.

tasks.prompt: A manhole in a Saskatchewan town is found with a tangle of rags, a mop head, and plastic bags blocking its outlet channel.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian manhole with dumped and flushed debris. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The mop head and bags are household items too large to pass a toilet trap.
An open maintenance hole cover was reported displaced the week before.
Upstream homes report no backups before the manhole blocked.
CCTV of the incoming pipes shows normal flow and no rag buildup.
Similar items are found in a nearby ditch beside the manhole.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Large items were dumped into the manhole through the displaced cover rather than flushed through the system
Residents flushed the items and they collected at the manhole
The items washed in from the upstream pipes during a storm
A cleaning crew left the items in the manhole by mistake

inference.explanation: Items too large for a toilet trap, a displaced cover the week before, clean incoming pipes, and matching items in the ditch all point to dumping at the manhole itself.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best supports the dumping conclusion for follow up?

options.label: Cover condition and security log with dated reports of the displaced cover, plus photos of the recovered items
Upstream CCTV report for the incoming pipes
Cleaning crew tool inventory

nextClue.explanation: The cover record establishes the access route that the oversized items needed.

clueText.nc-a: The log shows the cover reported displaced twice that week and photos show items that cannot pass a toilet trap.
clueText.nc-b: The incoming pipes already showed normal flow with no rag buildup.
clueText.nc-c: A tool inventory lists crew equipment, not household mop heads and bags.

tasks.prompt: Pumps at a small lift station in a foothills community clog with rags only after weekends, and weekday operation is normal.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian lift station with weekend ragging. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Recovered rags are mostly shop towels and cloth wipes.
A vehicle wash and workshop in the catchment operates mainly on weekends.
Dye checks show the workshop floor drain connects to the sanitary sewer.
Residential flow on weekdays carries no rags to the station.
Grease and grit levels in the wet well stay normal all week.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Residents flush more wipes on weekends than weekdays
Weekend workshop discharge through its floor drain is sending shop towels to the station
The pumps are weaker on weekends because of power supply dips
Roots grow into the wet well on weekends and shed fibres

inference.explanation: The rags are shop towels, the workshop runs on weekends and drains to the sanitary line, and weekday residential flow is rag free. Power dips would not deliver cloth, and residents would not supply shop towels.

nextClue.prompt: Which check best confirms the workshop pathway?

options.label: A household wipe survey in the catchment
Weekend inspection of the workshop drain and the first manhole below it during washdown, logging towels present
Voltage logging at the station over a weekend

nextClue.explanation: Finding shop towels at the workshop drain and the manhole below it during its operating hours closes the pathway.

clueText.nc-a: A household survey cannot explain industrial shop towels in the wet well.
clueText.nc-b: During Saturday washdown, shop towels are in the floor drain and matching towels appear in the manhole below.
clueText.nc-c: Voltage records describe power, not cloth arriving in the flow.

tasks.prompt: A sewer in a new subdivision in a western Canadian city blocks with pieces of pipe cutoffs, tape, and wood scraps six months after homes are occupied.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian new subdivision sewer with construction leftovers. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Jetting returns contain plastic pipe cutoffs, electrical tape, and wood scraps.
CCTV shows the debris resting at a manhole bench and at one low joint.
The subdivision sewers were never CCTV inspected at handover, unlike older areas.
No single home can be linked to the debris by dye testing.
Older subdivisions with handover inspection records do not show this debris pattern.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Residents are flushing renovation debris from many homes at once
The debris washed in from the storm system through a cross connection
Construction leftovers were left in the new sewers at build time and are now catching flow
Cleaning crews are leaving debris behind on each visit

inference.explanation: The material is building trade waste spread along the system, no home is linked, and the missing handover inspection is the gap that let it stay. Crews clean other areas without this pattern.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best supports requiring handover inspection on the next phase?

options.label: Dye test results for individual homes
Storm system CCTV for the subdivision
Debris inventory from this phase matched against the absent handover CCTV record for the same reaches

nextClue.explanation: Pairing what was found with the inspection step that was skipped makes the case for the requirement.

clueText.nc-a: Dye tests already failed to link any single home to the debris.
clueText.nc-b: No cross connection evidence is stated, and storm CCTV does not explain trade waste in sanitary reaches.
clueText.nc-c: The inventory lists trade waste in six reaches and the file shows no handover CCTV for any of them.

tasks.prompt: A care home sewer in British Columbia blocks monthly with wipes, while the rest of the street on the same main stays clear.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian care home lateral and main. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: CCTV shows wipe mats starting at the care home lateral connection and trailing downstream.
The main upstream of the connection is clean.
Care home staff confirm wipes are used for resident care and some are flushed.
Other homes on the street report no slow drains.
After staff training and bin changes, the next two monthly checks show no new mats.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The main is too small for the whole street and mats form everywhere
Roots at the connection are catching normal paper
Grease from the care home kitchen is forming the mats
Wipes flushed at the care home are entering at its lateral and matting in the main below it

inference.explanation: Mats start at the care home connection with a clean main above, staff confirm flushing, and training plus bins stops new mats. No roots or grease are reported, and other homes are unaffected.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best documents the improvement for the facility file?

options.label: Dated CCTV checks at the connection before and after the training and bin changes
Street wide backup counts for the year
Kitchen interceptor service records

nextClue.explanation: Before and after camera checks at the connection show whether mats stopped forming at the source.

clueText.nc-a: Checks show a heavy mat before the changes and a clean connection at both checks after.
clueText.nc-b: Street counts mix many causes and do not isolate the care home connection.
clueText.nc-c: Interceptor records cover kitchen grease, not wipes flushed in resident care.

tasks.prompt: A sewer reach below a watermain break in a prairie city fills with sand in the week after the break is repaired.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian sewer filling with sand after a watermain break. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Sand appears in the sewer only in the reach beside the break excavation.
CCTV shows a cracked sewer joint inside the excavation limits with sand entering.
Before the break, the same reach was clean on a routine camera run.
Sand volume decreases each week after the joint is exposed.
No construction site or open manhole is present on this street.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Break wash water and excavation disturbed the sewer joint, and sand is entering through the crack
Sand is entering through joints all over the old catchment at once
Residents are discharging sand into the sewer
The cleaning crew dragged sand in from the road surface

inference.explanation: Sand is limited to the excavation reach, a cracked joint is seen there with sand entering, and the reach was clean before the break. A catchment wide change would not start at one excavation in one week.

nextClue.prompt: Which check best confirms sand entry at the crack before repair?

options.label: Sand sampling from manholes across the catchment
Camera held at the cracked joint during a controlled water release in the excavation, logging sand movement at the crack
Resident discharge survey for the street

nextClue.explanation: Watching sand move at the crack during a controlled release directly proves the entry point.

clueText.nc-a: Catchment samples would dilute a signal already located at one crack.
clueText.nc-b: Sand pulses in at the crack as water is released and stops when the release stops.
clueText.nc-c: No resident activity explains sand limited to the excavation reach.

tasks.prompt: A gravity sewer in a valley town rags up at one protruding lateral connection, while smooth connections nearby stay clear.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian protruding connection catching wipes. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: CCTV shows one lateral connection sticking 50 mm into the main.
Wipes and rags hang from that connection and trail downstream.
Other connections in the same reach are flush and clean.
Flow above the connection is normal and the pipe barrel is sound.
Cutting the connection flush ends the ragging at follow up checks.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The whole reach receives far more wipes than nearby reaches
The protruding connection is snagging wipes that would otherwise pass through the reach
The pipe barrel is collapsing at the connection
Grease at the connection is gluing wipes in place

inference.explanation: Rags hang on the one protruding connection, flush connections stay clean, and removing the protrusion ends the problem. The barrel is sound and no grease is reported.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best supports the snag explanation in the repair file?

options.label: Wipe disposal survey for the catchment
Barrel thickness testing along the reach
CCTV stills of rags on the protruding connection and a clean follow up run after it was cut flush

nextClue.explanation: Before and after images at the same connection show the snag and its removal.

clueText.nc-a: A survey cannot explain why only the protruding connection collected rags.
clueText.nc-b: The barrel was already shown sound on camera.
clueText.nc-c: Stills show rags hanging on the protrusion and the follow up run shows the same spot clean.

tasks.prompt: A duplex lift station in a prairie town alarms on high level every night, and the lead pump is found not running each time.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian duplex lift station, night alarms. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The lead float hangs at its rest angle and does not tip when lifted by hand.
The lag pump starts normally on its own float and clears the well.
Motor tests on the lead pump are normal when it is started by hand.
Power supply and breaker checks are normal.
Swapping the float leads moves the fault to the other pump.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The lead pump motor has failed
The station power supply is failing at night
The lead start float has failed and is not calling the lead pump to start
Inflow at night is higher than both pumps can handle

inference.explanation: The pump runs by hand, power is normal, the lag pump clears the well alone, and the fault follows the float leads. That isolates the float, not the motor, power, or inflow.

nextClue.prompt: Which bench check best confirms the float fault before replacement?

options.label: Continuity test of the float switch while tipping it, logged against a known good float
A full load flow test of both pumps
A week of inflow logging at night

nextClue.explanation: A tipping continuity test shows whether the switch changes state, which is the failed function.

clueText.nc-a: The suspect float shows no continuity change when tipped, while the good float switches cleanly.
clueText.nc-b: Flow capacity is already shown adequate because the lag pump clears the well alone.
clueText.nc-c: Inflow logging does not test a switch that fails a hand tip test.

tasks.prompt: A lift station pump in Alberta runs for long periods but the wet well level falls very slowly.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian lift station with low pumping rate. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The pump motor current is well below its normal running value.
Discharge pressure at the pump is below the station normal range.
The impeller inspection shows heavy wear and a wide wear ring gap.
Floats, starter, and power supply all test normal.
The second pump in the station draws normal current and lowers the level at the normal rate.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The discharge line is fully blocked downstream
The float is calling for the pump to run at half speed
The wet well is filling faster than design inflow
The worn impeller and wear ring are letting flow slip back inside the pump, so output is low

inference.explanation: Low current, low pressure, and visible impeller wear fit internal slip, and the twin pump performs normally on the same well and discharge. A full blockage would raise pressure, not lower it.

nextClue.prompt: Which paired test best confirms internal slip before the pump is rebuilt?

options.label: A float tipping test on both floats
Timed drawdown test on each pump at the same well levels, with current and pressure logged for both
A power quality log for the station

nextClue.explanation: A same conditions drawdown comparison quantifies the weak pump against its healthy twin.

clueText.nc-a: Floats were already tested normal and both pumps start correctly.
clueText.nc-b: The worn pump takes three times as long to draw down and draws low current, while the twin matches its rated time.
clueText.nc-c: Power is shared by both pumps and the twin performs normally on it.

tasks.prompt: A wet well in a Manitoba town refills within minutes every time the pump stops, and the pump starts again almost right away.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian station with rapid refill after pumping. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Level falls at the normal rate while the pump runs.
Seconds after the pump stops, flow noise is heard in the discharge pipe.
The well refills to the start level in minutes with no inflow change at the inlet.
Holding the discharge valve closed by hand stops the refill.
Floats and pump output test normal.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The pump check valve is stuck open and pumped sewage is flowing back into the well
Inflow to the station has suddenly tripled
The stop float is set too close to the start float
The pump impeller is worn and cannot empty the well

inference.explanation: Normal pumping rate, return flow noise at stop, refill blocked by closing the discharge valve, and unchanged inlet flow all point to backflow through the check valve.

nextClue.prompt: Which check best confirms backflow through the check valve?

options.label: Inlet flow measurement over one day
Float level tape measurements
Close the discharge isolation valve at pump stop and log whether the refill stops, then reopen and log that it resumes

nextClue.explanation: Stopping and restarting the refill by valving the discharge is a direct backflow test.

clueText.nc-a: Inlet flow was already observed unchanged during the refill events.
clueText.nc-b: Float settings do not explain flow noise in the discharge pipe at pump stop.
clueText.nc-c: With the valve closed the level holds steady, and reopening brings the rapid refill back.

tasks.prompt: A lift station pump in a British Columbia town hums, trips its overload, and will not start, while its twin runs normally.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian single pump trips at one station. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Voltage checks show one of three supply phases at the failed pump starter is dead.
The twin pump starter shows all three phases present.
The failed pump motor windings test even and within range.
The overload trips within seconds each start attempt.
A fuse in one phase of the failed pump feeder is found blown.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The motor windings have burned out
Loss of one supply phase is preventing the motor from starting and tripping the overload
The impeller is seized solid with rags
The discharge check valve is stuck shut and locking the pump

inference.explanation: One dead phase with a blown fuse, even windings, and a healthy twin on its own starter fit single phasing. Burned windings would test uneven, and a seized impeller would not remove a supply phase.

nextClue.prompt: Which check best confirms the phase loss as the start failure cause?

options.label: Phase to phase voltage readings at the starter before and after the fuse is replaced, with a logged start test
A rag inspection of the impeller
A check valve stroke test

nextClue.explanation: Restoring the phase and logging a normal start ties the failure to the supply, not the pump.

clueText.nc-a: After the fuse is replaced all phases read even and the pump starts and runs at normal current.
clueText.nc-b: A rag inspection does not explain a dead phase at the starter.
clueText.nc-c: A stuck check valve would not blow a feeder fuse or remove a phase.

tasks.prompt: A lift station in a Saskatchewan town loses its pumping after every long idle weekend, and the pump runs but delivers nothing until it is primed.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian station losing prime after idle periods. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The pump is mounted above the wet well and draws through a suction line.
After running, the pump delivers at its normal rate.
A suction line joint above the water line is found damp and sucking air when the pump starts.
The foot valve at the suction inlet leaks back slowly when tested.
Weekday cycles are frequent and the pump never loses prime on weekdays.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The discharge check valve is stuck open and draining the well
The motor is losing power over weekends
Air leaking in at the suction joint and a leaking foot valve let the suction line drain during long idle periods
Inflow stops on weekends so the well goes dry

inference.explanation: Normal delivery once primed, a damp air leaking joint, and a foot valve that leaks back explain prime loss that needs idle time to develop. The well still has inflow, and the discharge side does not hold the suction charge.

nextClue.prompt: Which test best confirms the suction side leak path?

options.label: A discharge pressure log over a weekend
Isolated suction line hold test, filling the line and logging level drop with the suspect joint marked
A motor insulation test

nextClue.explanation: A hold test on the isolated suction line shows whether it keeps its charge and where it loses it.

clueText.nc-a: Discharge pressure is normal whenever the pump is primed and running.
clueText.nc-b: The line loses its fill in two hours and bubbles appear at the marked joint under test pressure.
clueText.nc-c: The motor runs normally once primed, so insulation does not explain prime loss.

tasks.prompt: At a duplex station in a western Canadian city, one pump has logged almost all the run hours for a year and the other pump looks new.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian duplex station with skewed run hours. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Both pumps start and run normally when selected by hand.
The automatic alternator relay is found stuck on one output.
Floats call correctly and the well cycles at normal intervals.
Run hour meters show a 95 to 5 split between the pumps.
No alarms have been recorded at the station in the year.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: One pump is much larger and the controls prefer it
The second pump is locked out by a fault that never alarms
Operators are manually selecting the same pump each visit
The alternator has failed in one position, so the same pump is selected every cycle

inference.explanation: Both pumps work by hand, floats call correctly, and the alternator relay is stuck on one output. Equal pumps with no lockout or alarms leave the stuck alternator as the cause of the hour split.

nextClue.prompt: Which logged test best confirms the alternator fault?

options.label: Compare pump nameplate sizes
Interview operators about manual selection
Force several start cycles with floats and log which pump the alternator selects each time

nextClue.explanation: Repeated automatic cycles show whether selection ever changes, which is the alternator job.

clueText.nc-a: Nameplates show the pumps are the same size, so size preference does not explain the split.
clueText.nc-b: Operator visits are monthly and cannot set selection on every daily cycle.
clueText.nc-c: Six forced cycles select the same pump every time, and selection changes only when the relay is replaced.

tasks.prompt: A lift station in a valley town high level alarms during a storm even though both pumps run the whole time.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian station wet weather alarms. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Both pumps run continuously and draw normal current with normal discharge pressure.
Timed drawdown tests last month matched the rated capacity of both pumps.
The wet well level still rises slowly during the storm peak.
Upstream flow monitoring shows storm inflow at four times dry weather flow.
Floats and alarms test correctly after the storm.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Storm inflow is exceeding the combined capacity of two healthy pumps
Both pumps have failed at the same time
The high level float is faulty and alarming early
The discharge line is blocked and no flow is leaving

inference.explanation: Both pumps run at normal current and pressure with proven capacity, yet the level rises while inflow is measured at four times normal. Healthy pumps plus excess inflow explain the alarm without any equipment fault.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best supports a capacity and inflow review rather than a pump repair?

options.label: Storm event log pairing upstream inflow, both pump run status, and wet well level over the peak hours
Pump repair quotes for both pumps
Float replacement record for the alarm float

nextClue.explanation: A paired event log shows capacity working as designed while inflow passes it, which directs the review.

clueText.nc-a: The log shows both pumps running at rated output while level rose with the four times inflow peak.
clueText.nc-b: Repair quotes assume a pump fault that current, pressure, and drawdown tests do not show.
clueText.nc-c: The alarm float tested correctly after the storm, and the level did rise to it.

tasks.prompt: A lift station in Alberta uses a bubbler tube for level control, and the displayed level stops changing while sewage keeps arriving.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian station with bubbler level sensing. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The control display holds one level reading for six hours.
A tape measure in the well shows the real level rising over the same period.
The backup float starts the pump at its set point and the display still does not change.
Air flow at the bubbler tube outlet is found blocked by a kinked and fouled line.
When the line is cleared, the display tracks the taped level again.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The wet well inflow stopped for six hours
The blocked bubbler line froze the level signal, so the controller could not see the rising level
The pump was removing exactly the inflow for six hours
The display unit failed and the sensing was fine

inference.explanation: The taped level rose, the backup float responded to real level, and clearing the bubbler line restored tracking. Inflow plainly continued, and the display worked once sensing was restored.

nextClue.prompt: Which check best documents the sensing fault for the station file?

options.label: Pump run time totals for the week
Paired log of taped level and displayed level before and after the bubbler line was cleared
Inflow estimate from upstream homes

clueText.nc-a: Run totals do not show what the level signal was doing.
clueText.nc-b: Before clearing, tape and display differ by a metre, and after clearing they agree within centimetres.

tasks.prompt: Clear looking water pools in the dry pit of a new lift station in a prairie town and the sump pump runs often.

Wet well sewage is seeping into the dry pit through the unsealed pipe sleeve
A potable water line in the pit is leaking

inference.explanation: Dye from the wet well reaching the pit, inflow tracking wet well level, and an unsealed sleeve give the pathway. The lack of odour fits diluted seepage, and rain has no effect, which argues against roof or groundwater entry.

nextClue.prompt: Which check best confirms the sleeve pathway before sealing?

options.label: Roof hatch hose test during dry weather
Potable line pressure test
Hold the wet well at a high level with the pit pumped dry and log the pit refill starting at the sleeve

tasks.prompt: A lift station pump in Manitoba trips on overload within a minute of starting, over and over, after a quiet month with no trips.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms ragging as the trip cause for the station log?

options.label: Start current log before and after cleaning, with photos of the material removed from the impeller
Overload relay calibration certificate
Voltage sag recording for the start

clueText.nc-a: Current is twice nameplate before cleaning and normal after, with photos of the rag mass removed.

clueText.nc-c: Voltage was already checked normal during the trips.

tasks.prompt: Flow at a prairie town treatment plant doubles within an hour of heavy rain starting and falls just as fast when rain stops.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian catchment with storm response. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The flow rise begins within an hour of rainfall starting.

A new subdivision has connected and doubled dry weather flow
The plant flow meter is drifting during storms

nextClue.prompt: Which test best confirms the roof leader share of the storm flow?

options.label: A month of groundwater level logging
Disconnect trial on a sample block during a storm, comparing flow response before and after the leaders are redirected
A dry weather flow audit of the new subdivision

nextClue.explanation: A storm trial with leaders redirected measures their direct contribution to the peak.

clueText.nc-a: Groundwater was already low, so logging it does not explain an hour scale response.
clueText.nc-b: With leaders redirected on the sample block, its storm peak falls by more than half while rainfall is similar.
clueText.nc-c: Dry weather flow was already steady, so a dry audit does not address storm peaks.

tasks.prompt: Sewer flows in a British Columbia coastal town stay high for three days after rain ends, and the extra water looks clear.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian catchment with delayed wet weather flow. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Flow peaks a day after the rain peak and declines slowly over three days.
Manhole inspection during the high flow shows clear water entering at pipe joints.
Groundwater monitoring wells near the sewer are at their seasonal high.
Roof leader dye tests on the catchment are negative.
The extra flow volume is far larger than the rain that fell on paved areas draining to manholes.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

Groundwater infiltration through joints is sustaining flow after the rain
A reservoir is overflowing into the sanitary system
Snowmelt from roofs is entering through vents

inference.explanation: A delayed, slow decline with clear water at joints, high groundwater, and negative roof dye tests fits infiltration. Direct inflow responds in minutes to hours, not days.

nextClue.prompt: Which paired record best confirms infiltration for the rehabilitation plan?

options.label: Roof leader inventory for the catchment
Reservoir level records for the week
Flow hydrograph paired with groundwater levels and joint entry observations over one storm cycle

nextClue.explanation: Pairing the slow flow tail with groundwater height and visible joint entry ties the extra water to infiltration.

clueText.nc-a: Roof dye tests were already negative across the catchment.
clueText.nc-b: No reservoir overflow is stated, and the timing follows groundwater, not a reservoir event.
clueText.nc-c: Flow stays high while groundwater is high and falls as groundwater falls, with clear entry seen at joints.

tasks.prompt: Night flows in a dry week in a Saskatchewan town stay at 70 percent of average daytime flow, far above the expected night minimum.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian night flow analysis. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The high night flow occurs in a dry week with no rain.
Legitimate night water use in the catchment is small, mostly a hospital and a bakery.

Steady groundwater infiltration in the old reach is holding night flow up
A trunk sewer from another town is connected at night only

nextClue.prompt: Which measurement best quantifies the infiltration for the repair program?

options.label: Reach by reach night isolation, damming and measuring flow at manholes through the old reach at 3 a.m.
A resident water use survey
A daytime flow comparison of the two reaches

tasks.prompt: During storms, a manhole in a road dip in a Calgary neighbourhood is found with water jetting in around its cover while nearby manholes stay dry at the rim.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian manhole in a road dip. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The manhole sits in a dip where storm water ponds to 150 mm depth.

The sewer is surcharging and pushing water out of the cover
A storm drain cross connection feeds this manhole
Ponded storm water is entering through this manhole cover and frame, a direct inflow point

nextClue.prompt: Which trial best confirms the cover entry point?

options.label: A joint CCTV run below the manhole
Controlled ponding trial with dyed water over the cover, watching for dye inside the manhole
A storm drain dye test on the street

tasks.prompt: A home in a Manitoba town gets sanitary backups only when it rains, and its neighbours on a separate storm street stay dry.

The home storm sump discharges to the sanitary lateral, found by dye test.
Dry weather flows at the home are normal.
Neighbours without these connections do not back up in the same storms.
The sanitary main itself shows no defect on CCTV.

Dye test log for the roof leader and the sump, with times and photos, tied to the property record

tasks.prompt: Spring melt in a prairie town sends sewer flows to triple the winter average for two weeks, peaking each afternoon and easing each night.

nextClue.prompt: Which observation best confirms the melt pathway for next year planning?

Industrial discharge permits issued that spring

tasks.prompt: A sewer crossing under a creek in a foothills town shows flow gains that rise and fall with creek level, not with rain on the town.

Simultaneous flow measurement above and below the crossing through one creek rise, paired with the joint CCTV log
Pump station cycle records

tasks.prompt: After a catchment in Edmonton is lined and its manholes sealed, dry weather flow at the plant falls by a quarter and stays down.

Night flows fall the most, while daytime use flows change little.

The lining and sealing removed groundwater infiltration that had been a large share of dry flow

Before and after night flow comparison for the lined catchment at similar groundwater levels

tasks.prompt: A new subdivision in a western Canadian city shows storm flow spikes from day one, and dry weather flow is normal.

A joint pressure test of the new sewers
A design flow recalculation for the subdivision

tasks.prompt: Two subcatchments of similar size in a Saskatchewan city show very different storm responses, and crews must decide where rehabilitation money goes first.

The difference is caused by rainfall varying between the areas
Both areas are equal priority because their sizes match

A single storm flow reading for area A

tasks.prompt: After root cutting in a clay sewer in a prairie town, flow improves for a day, then the reach blocks again with soil and small stones in the returns.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian sewer after root cutting. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: First day returns after cutting are roots only and flow is restored.
Second day returns contain soil, sand, and small stones along with roots.

A shallow depression has formed in the boulevard above the same joint.
Upstream reaches return only roots when cut.

Roots alone regrew overnight and blocked the pipe again
The joint has displaced and soil is entering the pipe, so the blockage is now structural
The cutter left root debris that washed back into a ball

inference.explanation: Soil and stones in returns, soil visible behind an open displaced joint, and a surface depression all point to soil entry through a failed joint. Roots cannot regrow overnight, and upstream grit would not bring soil from behind the wall.

nextClue.prompt: Which check best confirms soil entry before excavation is planned?

A grease sample from the downstream manhole
Still camera log of the joint during flow, showing soil grains dropping from the joint gap

tasks.prompt: Rodding a blocked reach in a Manitoba town brings back roots mixed with pieces of orange clay pipe.

The pipe is 60 year old clay in the affected section and sound clay elsewhere.

Flow returns to normal in the sound sections after rodding.

Roots alone have grown thick enough to break the rodding cable
The pipe wall has failed at that section and roots are entering through the break

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best defines the repair limits before digging?

A chemical root treatment of the whole reach
A flow study of the upstream catchment

clueText.nc-b: Root treatment cannot restore a missing pipe wall.

tasks.prompt: A plastic sewer in a new Alberta subdivision shows a flattened top on CCTV along one short section, while the rest of the pipe is round.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian plastic pipe with shape change. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The flattened section is directly below a driveway crossing.

Deflection measurements at the crossing section paired with the bedding record and the round sections elsewhere
Crawler weight specifications

tasks.prompt: A concrete sewer crown in a coastal town is soft and crumbling above the waterline, while the submerged wall is hard and sound.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian concrete sewer with crown damage. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Damage is worst at the crown and stops at the normal waterline.
Gas readings at the manhole show hydrogen sulfide present in the air space.
The reach has long, slow flow from a flat upstream section.
Newer plastic reaches on the same system show no wall damage.
The submerged concrete tests hard with a hammer sounding.

Surface pH test of the moist crown wall paired with sulfide gas logging in the air space

tasks.prompt: A manhole in a Winnipeg neighbourhood has a broken channel and benching, and deposits build up inside the manhole while the pipes stay clean.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best supports a benching repair rather than more cleaning?

options.label: Photo log of deposits lodged on the broken bench across two inspections, with the smooth neighbour manhole for comparison

Flow capacity calculation for the manhole

nextClue.explanation: Photos of deposits sitting on the defect, against a clean smooth comparison, justify repair over repeat cleaning.

tasks.prompt: CCTV in a Saskatchewan sewer shows one joint stepped inward by 30 mm, and debris hangs up at that joint on every run.

Joints upstream and downstream of this one are flush.

Measured offset log with stills of the lip and the debris hang up, tied to distance from the manhole
A resident wipe survey for the reach
