tasks.prompt: A sewer camera in a prairie town goes under water in the middle of a reach and comes up again before the next manhole, on a dry day.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian sewer with a mid reach low section. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Depth in the pipe is normal at both manholes.
The submerged section is about 15 m long.
Deposits of grit and paper line the submerged section.
Dye travel time through the reach is much slower than the grade suggests.
No blockage is found at the downstream manhole.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: A sag or belly in the pipe holds water and slows flow through the middle of the reach
The downstream sewer is surcharged and backing water up the reach
The camera is sinking because its cable is too short
Groundwater is flooding the pipe at mid reach

inference.explanation: Normal depth at both ends, a defined mid reach pond, deposits, and slow dye travel fit a belly holding water. Surcharge would raise levels at the downstream manhole too, and no downstream blockage is found.

nextClue.prompt: Which survey best confirms the belly for the repair plan?

options.label: A downstream surcharge level log
A camera cable length check
Invert level survey through the reach showing the low section between the two manholes

nextClue.explanation: An invert survey shows the low section directly and sizes the repair.

clueText.nc-a: Downstream levels were normal, so a surcharge log would not explain a mid reach pond.
clueText.nc-b: Cable length does not change dye travel time or deposit patterns.
clueText.nc-c: The survey shows inverts dipping 80 mm below grade for 15 m mid reach.

tasks.prompt: A manhole in a British Columbia town shows white and grey streaks running down its walls from the frame, and the channel flow is clear at night.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian manhole frame and wall leakage. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Streaks start at the frame joint and run down the chimney section.
At night, clear water trickles from the same joint while homes are asleep.
Pipe joints entering the manhole are dry on inspection.
Groundwater around the manhole is high in spring, when the trickle is strongest.
The streak pattern matches mineral deposits left by evaporated seepage.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Sewage is splashing up the walls from the channel
Groundwater is leaking into the manhole at the frame and chimney joint
Rain is running down the inside of the cover only
Condensation alone is forming the streaks and trickle

inference.explanation: Streaks and a night trickle start at the frame joint, pipe joints are dry, and the flow follows groundwater season. Splash would centre on the channel, and condensation does not produce a running trickle.

nextClue.prompt: Which check best confirms the frame joint as the leak path?

options.label: Dry the chimney, then watch the joint during a high groundwater period with the cover sealed test logged
A channel splash observation at peak flow
A cover rain test with a hose

nextClue.explanation: Watching the joint itself leak in high groundwater, with rain excluded, isolates the path.

clueText.nc-a: With the cover sealed against rain, clear water still beads and runs from the frame joint.
clueText.nc-b: Splash was ruled out by streaks starting above the channel at the frame.
clueText.nc-c: A hose test checks rain entry, but the trickle runs in dry weather too.

tasks.prompt: A sewer pipe in an Alberta town is sheared and cracked right where it enters a manhole, and the pipe beyond is sound for its full length.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian pipe crack at manhole entry. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The crack rings the pipe within 0.5 m of the manhole wall.
The manhole has settled slightly relative to the surrounding road.
CCTV shows the rest of the pipe round, aligned, and free of cracks.
Soil fines are entering at the crack.
A flexible connector was not used at this connection, unlike newer manholes nearby.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The pipe material is defective along its whole length
Tree roots have crushed the pipe at the manhole
Differential settlement between the manhole and the pipe is shearing the pipe at the entry
Cleaning equipment cracked the pipe at its weakest point by chance

inference.explanation: Damage confined to the entry ring, a settled manhole, sound pipe beyond, and no flexible connector fit settlement shear. A material defect would show elsewhere, and no roots are reported at the crack.

nextClue.prompt: Which comparison best supports a flexible connector retrofit?

options.label: Pipe material test results for the whole reach
Crack location log for this manhole against newer manholes with connectors that show no entry cracks
Root inspection of the connection

nextClue.explanation: Comparing settled entries with and without connectors tests the settlement explanation.

clueText.nc-a: Material tests do not explain damage only at the entry ring.
clueText.nc-b: Older rigid entries on the street show entry cracks, and connector entries show none at similar ages.
clueText.nc-c: No roots were found at this crack on inspection.

tasks.prompt: An older brick manhole in a Manitoba town is losing mortar and bricks are bulging into the shaft, while its concrete pipes are sound.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian brick manhole inspection. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Mortar joints in the brickwork are soft and can be scraped out by hand.
Several bricks have shifted inward above the benching.
Gas readings in the shaft show hydrogen sulfide present.
The pipes entering the manhole show no wall loss.
The same age concrete manholes nearby show surface softening but no bulging.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The entering pipes are failing and pushing the bricks inward
Traffic loads alone have crushed the shaft in one season
The benching is causing the brickwork to bulge
The brick manhole structure is deteriorating and losing its shape, and it is the asset that needs repair

inference.explanation: Soft mortar, shifted bricks, and sound pipes put the failure in the manhole structure itself. Pipes cannot push bricks inward when they show no damage, and one season of traffic does not soften mortar throughout the shaft.

nextClue.prompt: Which assessment best scopes the manhole repair?

options.label: CCTV report for the entering pipes
Traffic count for the street
Full shaft condition log with mortar depth loss and brick displacement measured by course

nextClue.explanation: A course by course shaft log sizes the structural repair that is actually needed.

clueText.nc-a: CCTV already showed the entering pipes sound.
clueText.nc-b: Traffic counts do not measure mortar loss or brick movement.
clueText.nc-c: The log records mortar loss to 25 mm depth and inward brick shift on six courses.

tasks.prompt: Sewage spills from a manhole in a dry week in a prairie town, and the spill stops on its own before crews arrive.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian dry weather manhole spill. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: No rain fell in the five days before the spill.
CCTV below the spill manhole finds a dense root mass blocking most of the pipe.
Upstream of the root mass the pipe is surcharged, and downstream it runs at normal depth.
The spill volume matches the hours the root mass held flow back, estimated from upstream levels.
No lift station or pump is present on this gravity reach.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The downstream root blockage surcharged the reach and spilled at the lowest manhole
A lift station failure upstream caused the spill
Storm inflow overloaded the whole catchment
The manhole cover was left off and sewage splashed out

inference.explanation: Dry weather, a root mass with surcharge above and normal flow below, and no pumps on the reach isolate the blockage as the spill cause.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best completes the spill report cause section?

options.label: CCTV log of the root mass with upstream and downstream depth readings taken the same day
Rainfall records for the spill week
Lift station alarm history for the town

nextClue.explanation: The paired depths around the located blockage document the spill mechanism for the report.

clueText.nc-a: Depths show surcharge above the mass and normal flow below it, with the mass logged at a fixed distance.
clueText.nc-b: The week was dry, so rainfall records cannot explain this spill.
clueText.nc-c: There is no lift station on this gravity reach to alarm.

tasks.prompt: A lift station in a Saskatchewan town spills during a winter power outage, and the wet well overflows before power returns.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian station outage overflow. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Both pumps stop when the utility power fails.
The standby generator starts, runs for two minutes, and shuts down on low coolant.
High level alarms are recorded but no pump runs during the outage.
Inflow continues at normal dry weather rates during the outage.
After power returns, the pumps clear the well at normal rates with no faults.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: A pump failed mechanically during the outage and caused the spill
The outage plus the generator shutdown left the station with no pumping, so normal inflow filled and overflowed the well
Storm inflow during the outage exceeded station capacity
The discharge line froze and blocked all pumping

inference.explanation: Pumps work normally after power returns, inflow was at dry weather rates, and the generator shutdown is logged. The spill needs no pump fault or storm, only hours without any pumping.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best supports the spill cause for the follow up on the generator?

options.label: Pump repair invoice for the station
Event timeline pairing the outage, generator run and shutdown alarms, and well level to the overflow time
Storm rainfall totals for the outage day

nextClue.explanation: A timeline showing no pumping from generator shutdown to power return establishes the cause chain.

clueText.nc-a: Pump invoices would suggest a mechanical fault, but both pumps ran normally after power returned.
clueText.nc-b: The timeline shows the generator stopping at minute two and the well rising steadily to overflow.
clueText.nc-c: The day had dry weather inflow, so rainfall totals do not explain the overflow.

tasks.prompt: A force main in an Alberta town is suspected of leaking, and wet ground appears along its route while station flows look normal.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian force main leak investigation. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: A wet, odorous patch grows along the force main alignment at a low point.
Pumped volume at the station exceeds volume arriving at the discharge manhole by a steady margin.
Station pressure is slightly below its normal range at the usual flow.
The gravity sewers nearby are at normal depth and show no surcharge.
Dye placed in the force main discharge test appears in the wet patch soil water.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: A gravity sewer nearby is surcharging and spilling at the patch
Groundwater is simply rising at a low point in the field
The force main is leaking at the low point and losing pumped sewage to the ground
The station meter is over reading and no water is lost

inference.explanation: A volume loss between station and discharge, low pressure, a growing odorous patch on the alignment, and force main dye in the patch water all fit a leak. Nearby gravity sewers are normal, and plain groundwater would not carry the dye.

nextClue.prompt: Which check best locates the leak for excavation?

options.label: CCTV of the nearby gravity sewers
Groundwater level readings in the field
Step pressure and flow comparison along the main with acoustic listening at the wet patch

nextClue.explanation: Acoustic and pressure stepping along the main pinpoint the loss point the volume balance already proves.

clueText.nc-a: Gravity sewers were already at normal depth with no surcharge.
clueText.nc-b: Groundwater readings do not explain dye from the force main in the patch.
clueText.nc-c: Listening peaks at the wet patch and pressure steps down across that section.

tasks.prompt: Sewage surfaces in a ditch beside a road in a British Columbia town hours after a directional drilling crew works nearby.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian sewer damaged by drilling. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The drilling crew crossed the sewer alignment that morning, shown on their bore log.
Flow in the sewer below the crossing drops while upstream levels rise.
Excavation at the crossing finds the bore hole through the sewer pipe wall.
Sewage in the ditch matches the timing of the bore crossing.
No rain fell and no other work was done on the sewer that day.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The sewer collapsed from old age the same day by coincidence
A storm cross connection is discharging to the ditch
The ditch water is groundwater made odorous by soil
The drill bore struck the sewer and sewage is escaping through the bore hole

inference.explanation: The bore log crossing, flow changes at the crossing, and the excavated bore hole in the pipe wall give a direct cause. Coincidence collapse would not leave a clean bore hole matching the drill path.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best supports the damage claim against the drilling work?

options.label: Bore log overlaid on the sewer alignment with excavation photos of the hole in the pipe
Pipe age records for the sewer
Rainfall records for the week

nextClue.explanation: Overlaying the drill path on the alignment with photos of the matching hole is the direct evidence.

clueText.nc-a: The overlay shows the bore crossing at the exact chainage where the holed pipe was excavated.
clueText.nc-b: Pipe age does not explain a fresh bore hole on the drill path.
clueText.nc-c: The day was dry, so rainfall does not explain sewage in the ditch.

tasks.prompt: A manhole near a creek in a Manitoba town spills during jetting of a grease reach upstream, then stops when jetting stops.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian spill during cleaning. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The spill manhole is the lowest manhole between the jetting point and a known grease restriction.
Spill timing matches jetting runs minute by minute.
Dry weather flow before jetting was at normal depth everywhere.
When jetting pauses, the manhole level falls back within minutes.
The grease restriction is later measured at about half the pipe area.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Jetting flow could not pass the grease restriction, surcharged the reach, and spilled at the low manhole
A storm drain cross connection opened during jetting
The manhole was already spilling before crews arrived
The downstream trunk sewer collapsed during the work

inference.explanation: Minute by minute timing with jetting, normal levels before, fast recovery on pauses, and a half blocked restriction fit cleaning surcharge. A trunk collapse would not recover when jetting pauses.

nextClue.prompt: Which change best prevents a repeat at the next cleaning?

options.label: Jet at higher flow to finish faster
Clean from the downstream side first and reduce jetting flow, with a watcher and vacuum truck at the low manhole
Move the spill report to the next day paperwork only

nextClue.explanation: Opening the restriction from downstream and controlling added flow removes the surcharge mechanism.

clueText.nc-a: Higher flow adds water against the same restriction and worsens surcharge.
clueText.nc-b: Cleaning downstream first opens the path, and the watcher with vacuum cover catches any rise at the low manhole.
clueText.nc-c: Paperwork timing does not change the hydraulics that caused the spill.

tasks.prompt: A winter spill in a prairie town comes from a manhole on a shallow sewer near a creek crossing, during a cold snap at minus 30 degrees.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian winter spill at shallow sewer. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The sewer at the crossing has only 1 m of cover and is exposed to cold air at the creek bank.
CCTV after thawing shows a solid ice section at the crossing and clear pipe elsewhere.
Upstream flow was normal sanitary flow, with no storm or melt event.
The spill stopped after steam thawing opened a channel through the ice section.
The same crossing froze in a previous cold snap three years earlier.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Roots grew suddenly during the cold snap and blocked the pipe
Ice formed in the shallow crossing section and blocked flow until it was thawed
A pump station upstream pushed excess flow to the manhole
The manhole cover was frozen off by ice pressure

inference.explanation: Ice seen in the pipe at the shallow crossing, normal inflow, relief by thawing, and a repeat history at the same spot in cold snaps all fit freezing. Roots do not grow in a cold snap, and no pump station feeds this gravity reach.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best supports insulation work at the crossing?

options.label: Root treatment records for the reach
Pump station run records upstream
Freeze history log pairing cold snap dates, ice locations from CCTV, and cover depth at the crossing

nextClue.explanation: A history tying ice to the shallow, cold exposed section justifies insulating that section.

clueText.nc-a: Root records do not explain ice photographed inside the pipe.
clueText.nc-b: No pump station feeds this gravity reach.
clueText.nc-c: The log shows ice at the same crossing in both cold snaps, where cover is only 1 m.

tasks.prompt: A lift station in a western Canadian town reports pumps running all day, yet the well overflows in dry weather.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian station overflow with pumps running. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Both pumps run and draw current, but discharge flow at the outlet manhole is near zero.
Well level does not fall while the pumps run.
A shared discharge header valve between the pumps is found almost fully closed after maintenance.
Opening the header valve restores normal discharge and the well draws down.
Inflows are at normal dry weather rates throughout.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Both pump impellers wore out on the same day
Dry weather inflow suddenly exceeded station capacity
The partly closed header valve blocked discharge, so running pumps could not empty the well
The floats failed and never called the pumps

inference.explanation: Pumps running with near zero discharge, a found closed header valve, and instant recovery on opening it explain the overflow. Floats plainly called the pumps, and inflow never changed.

nextClue.prompt: Which practice record best prevents a repeat after maintenance?

options.label: Post maintenance valve position checklist signed off with a discharge flow verification run
Pump impeller inspection schedule
Float replacement record for the station

nextClue.explanation: A valve position sign off with a flow check catches a closed header before the station is left.

clueText.nc-a: The checklist records every valve position and a timed discharge run before the crew leaves site.
clueText.nc-b: Impellers were moving water as soon as the valve opened, so wear was not the cause.
clueText.nc-c: Floats called the pumps correctly all day, so replacement is not the lesson.

tasks.prompt: A restaurant block sewer in Edmonton spills at a manhole on a busy Saturday, and the spill is dark and greasy.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian grease spill at restaurant block. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: CCTV below the spill manhole shows a grease mat blocking about two thirds of the pipe.
Upstream of the mat the pipe is surcharged, and downstream it runs shallow.
One restaurant interceptor on the block is overdue for service by six months.
Dry weather flow volumes are normal for the block.
Jetting the mat restores flow and the spill does not return after interceptor service resumes.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Saturday customer volume alone overwhelmed a clear pipe
A root mass blocked the pipe below the manhole
The manhole was venting a downstream trunk surcharge
The grease mat from the block, fed by the overdue interceptor, blocked the pipe and spilled at the manhole

inference.explanation: A located grease mat with surcharge above and shallow flow below, an overdue interceptor, and no return after cleaning and service all fit grease. Roots are not seen, and normal dry flow cannot overwhelm a clear pipe.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best closes the spill file with cause and correction?

options.label: Saturday sales records for the restaurants
CCTV log of the mat with depths above and below it, paired with the interceptor service record after the spill
Trunk sewer level records for the city

nextClue.explanation: Pairing the located blockage with the source correction documents both cause and fix.

clueText.nc-a: Sales records show customers, not what blocked the pipe.
clueText.nc-b: The file pairs the mat log and depth readings with the interceptor service completed that week.
clueText.nc-c: Trunk levels do not explain a mat photographed in this reach with shallow flow below it.

tasks.prompt: Sewage spills from a cleanout in a low yard in a Saskatchewan town each time the city flushes the main on the street.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian spill at yard cleanout during flushing. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The yard cleanout cap is cracked and sits below the street manhole rim.
Spills happen only during main flushing and stop when flushing stops.
A partial root restriction is found in the main just below the home connection.
Normal dry weather flow causes no spill at the cleanout.
Neighbouring yards with sound caps and no restriction do not spill.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Flushing flow surcharging at the root restriction escapes at the low, cracked cleanout, the weakest exit on the reach
The home lateral is fully blocked at all times
Groundwater pressure is pushing sewage out of the cleanout
The flushing crew is pumping water directly into the lateral

inference.explanation: Spills only during flushing, a cracked low cap, and a partial restriction below the connection fit surcharge finding the weak exit. A full lateral block would spill in normal flow too.

nextClue.prompt: Which repair pairing best addresses both parts of this spill path?

options.label: Replace the cleanout cap only and flush at full flow
Cut the roots only and leave the cap as found
Cut the root restriction in the main and replace the cracked cleanout cap, then retest with a flushing run

nextClue.explanation: The spill needs both the surcharge source and the weak exit fixed, proven by a retest.

clueText.nc-a: A cap alone leaves the restriction surcharging the reach on every flush.
clueText.nc-b: Cutting roots alone leaves a cracked low cap as the next spill point in any surcharge.
clueText.nc-c: With roots cut and a sound cap fitted, the retest flushing run produces no spill at the yard.

tasks.prompt: A spill in a coastal town is first blamed on a storm, but the spill began six hours before any rain fell.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian spill timing investigation. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The spill start time is logged by a level alarm at 2 a.m., and rain began at 8 a.m.
CCTV after the spill finds a collapsed pipe section below the spill manhole.
Upstream flow was at normal night rates when the spill began.
Debris and soil are packed in the pipe below the collapsed section.
Neighbouring catchments with the same rain did not spill that night.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Storm inflow started the spill and the alarm clock was wrong
The pipe collapse blocked flow and started the spill hours before the storm arrived
Roots blocked the pipe at the moment the rain started
The storm surcharged every catchment equally that night

inference.explanation: The alarm timeline, a found collapse with packed soil, and normal night flow put the blockage first. Other catchments took the same rain without spilling, so the storm alone is not the cause.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best defends the cause finding if the storm claim is disputed?

options.label: Alarm and rainfall timeline aligned to the hour, paired with the collapse CCTV log
Total rainfall for the storm day
A root treatment quote for the reach

nextClue.explanation: An aligned timeline plus the located collapse separates the two events cleanly.

clueText.nc-a: The aligned record shows the spill at 2 a.m. in dry weather and the collapse logged below the manhole.
clueText.nc-b: Daily rainfall totals hide the six hour gap that decides this case.
clueText.nc-c: No root mass was found, so a root quote does not address the collapse.

tasks.prompt: Odour complaints cluster at one drop manhole in a prairie city, while manholes upstream and downstream draw no complaints.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian drop manhole odour cluster. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Sewage falls about 2 m inside the drop manhole and splashes into the channel.
Hydrogen sulfide readings are highest inside this manhole and low at its neighbours.
Upstream sewage arrives septic after a long, flat reach.
Complaints peak on warm afternoons.
Sealing the cover gaps reduces complaints while a repair is planned.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: A dead animal in the manhole is causing the odour
An industry upstream discharges odorous waste only at this manhole
Turbulence at the drop is stripping dissolved sulfide out of septic sewage into the manhole air
The manhole is venting the whole city sewer system

inference.explanation: Septic inflow, a 2 m turbulent drop, sulfide highest at this structure, and warm afternoon peaks fit gas stripping at the drop. An upstream discharge would affect upstream manholes too, and no animal is reported.

nextClue.prompt: Which measurement best confirms the stripping explanation?

options.label: An industrial discharge audit for the catchment
Sulfide readings in the incoming sewage and in manhole air, logged at this manhole and a quiet upstream manhole
A cover count survey for the street

nextClue.explanation: Comparing dissolved sulfide and air readings at the drop and at a quiet manhole tests the stripping step.

clueText.nc-a: An audit does not explain why only the drop manhole draws complaints.
clueText.nc-b: Dissolved sulfide is similar at both manholes, but air sulfide is ten times higher at the drop.
clueText.nc-c: Cover counts do not measure gas release at the drop.

tasks.prompt: A gravity manhole below a long force main discharge in an Alberta town smells strongly, while the rest of the system draws few complaints.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian force main discharge odour. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The force main is several kilometres long and sewage sits in it for hours between pump runs.
Odour at the discharge manhole spikes right after each pump run ends.
Hydrogen sulfide readings at the manhole are high, and readings fall with distance downstream.
The gravity sewers upstream of the lift station draw no complaints.
Odour is worst in summer when sewage is warmest.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The gravity sewer below the manhole is blocked and stagnant
A nearby industry discharges at the manhole itself
The lift station wet well is the odour source venting through the main
Sewage goes septic in the long force main and releases sulfide gas when it discharges turbulently at the manhole

inference.explanation: Long detention, odour spikes timed to pump runs, and sulfide falling downstream fit septic force main discharge. A blocked gravity sewer would show surcharge, and no industry connection at the manhole is stated.

nextClue.prompt: Which log best confirms the force main detention explanation?

options.label: Gravity sewer CCTV below the manhole
Industrial discharge permits near the manhole
Pump run times paired with sulfide readings at the discharge manhole over several cycles

nextClue.explanation: Pairing readings to pump cycles tests whether discharge events bring the odour with them.

clueText.nc-a: Gravity CCTV checks blockage, but no surcharge or blockage is reported at the manhole.
clueText.nc-b: Permits do not time odour spikes to pump runs.
clueText.nc-c: Sulfide peaks within minutes of each pump stop and fades between runs, matching force main slugs.

tasks.prompt: A homeowner in a Winnipeg suburb reports sewer odour inside the house, but no odour is found at the street manholes.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian indoor odour at one home. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The home basement floor drain trap is found dry.
Odour is strongest beside the floor drain and fades when the trap is filled with water.
Street manholes and neighbouring homes report no odour.
The home lateral and main are flowing normally.
The home was vacant for two months before the complaint, with no water use.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The dry floor drain trap let sewer gas enter the house from its own lateral
The street sewer is generating unusual gas that targets this house
A blockage in the main is pushing gas into all nearby homes
The home water heater is producing the odour

inference.explanation: A dry trap after two months vacant, odour at the drain, and instant improvement on filling it isolate the trap. A main problem would affect neighbours and the street manholes.

nextClue.prompt: Which simple check best confirms the trap explanation for the resident file?

options.label: Fill the trap, add a little mineral oil to slow evaporation, and recheck odour at the drain over the next week
CCTV of the street main
Gas readings at the street manholes

nextClue.explanation: Refilling the trap and watching the odour stay gone tests the pathway directly.

clueText.nc-a: Odour is gone the same day the trap is filled and stays gone at the one week recheck.
clueText.nc-b: The main was already flowing normally with no street odour.
clueText.nc-c: Street readings were already normal and would not test this home trap.

tasks.prompt: Odour complaints in a British Columbia subdivision peak every summer afternoon and are faint all winter, near a low wet area with slow sewers.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian subdivision odour in summer. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The subdivision sewers are flat and flow is slow and deep.
Sewage temperatures are highest on summer afternoons.
Sulfide readings at manholes track sewage temperature through the day.
No new industry or restaurant has opened in the subdivision.
Winter complaints are rare at the same manholes.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Residents open windows in summer and simply notice odour more
Warm, slow sewage is generating more sulfide in summer, so odour follows temperature
A seasonal industry starts up each summer in the subdivision
Roots die in summer and release odour as they decay

inference.explanation: Sulfide readings, not just complaints, track temperature, and no seasonal source exists. Noticing more would not raise instrument readings, and root decay is not a sulfide source of this pattern.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best supports a summer odour control step for this area?

options.label: A resident survey on window opening habits
Seasonal sulfide and temperature log at the complaint manholes across summer and winter
An industry startup registry for the subdivision

nextClue.explanation: A matched instrument log shows the generation pattern that control must address.

clueText.nc-a: A survey measures noticing, not the sulfide the instruments recorded.
clueText.nc-b: The log shows sulfide doubling on warm afternoons and near zero in winter at the same manholes.
clueText.nc-c: No industry startup is stated in the subdivision.

tasks.prompt: After a sewer reach in a prairie town is cleaned for the first time in years, odour complaints nearby rise for two weeks, then fade.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian post cleaning odour effect. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The reach had heavy slime and deposit layers before cleaning.
Cleaning removed the deposits and exposed bare pipe and fresh sewage surfaces.
No new discharges began in the area during those two weeks.
Complaints fade as a normal slime layer re forms on the cleaned pipe.
Sulfide readings follow the same rise and fall pattern as the complaints.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: A new industry began discharging during the cleaning week
The cleaning crew damaged the pipe and sewage is leaking
Cleaning disturbed the reach and temporarily raised sulfide release until the pipe surface settled again
Residents only imagined odour because they saw the trucks

On the checked reach, the camera found a missed grease shelf and the crew made a second pass the same day.
On the unchecked reach, no second pass was made.
The checked reach stays clear for a year, and the unchecked reach blocks in two months.
Discharge sources on both reaches are similar restaurants.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The unchecked reach restaurants discharge more grease
The verification pass caught leftover grease that would have reseeded the blockage, so verification is the difference
The checked reach pipe is newer and resists grease
Random chance explains a two month versus one year result

inference.explanation: Same crew, settings, loads, and sources leave the found and removed grease shelf as the working difference. Chance is weak against a photographed shelf removed on one reach only.

nextClue.prompt: Which program record best captures the lesson for other reaches?

options.label: Cleaning log pairing post cleaning CCTV findings and second pass actions with months of clear service after
Crew timesheets for the cleaning week
Restaurant counts on both reaches

nextClue.explanation: Pairing what verification found and fixed with the service outcome is the transferable lesson.

clueText.nc-a: The log shows the shelf found and removed on the checked reach, then twelve clear months against two.
clueText.nc-b: Timesheets show hours, not the shelf the camera found and the second pass removed.
clueText.nc-c: Restaurant counts were already similar and do not explain the outcome gap.

tasks.prompt: During cleaning of a long reach in a Saskatchewan town, a backup occurs at a mid reach home, and the crew learns the reach was cleaned from the top down.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian cleaning sequence problem. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The crew jetted from the upstream manhole toward a known downstream restriction.
Debris loosened upstream collected at the restriction and raised levels mid reach.
The mid reach home is the lowest connection on the reach.
When the downstream section was cleaned first on the next visit, no backup occurred.
Flow and weather were similar on both visits.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The home lateral failed on the first visit by coincidence
Jetting water volume alone always causes backups on this reach
Cleaning upstream first pushed debris into the downstream restriction and surcharged the reach
The restriction grew suddenly during the first visit

inference.explanation: Debris delivered to a known restriction, a low mid reach home, and a clean result when the order was reversed fit sequence as the cause. The same water volume caused no problem on the second visit.

nextClue.prompt: Which standing instruction best prevents a repeat?

options.label: Always jet at maximum flow to finish long reaches quickly
Clean long reaches from the downstream end upward, clearing restrictions first, with levels watched at low connections
Skip the downstream section when it looks partly open

nextClue.explanation: Opening the downstream path first gives loosened debris somewhere to go.

clueText.nc-a: Maximum flow delivers debris to a restriction faster and raises levels sooner.
clueText.nc-b: Working upward from a cleared downstream end keeps levels normal at the low home on the next cleaning.
clueText.nc-c: Skipping the downstream section leaves the restriction that caused the surcharge.

tasks.prompt: A sewer in a foothills town is reported cleaned, but a camera audit finds the jetting hose marks show it stopped 20 m short of the far manhole.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian cleaning audit by hose marks. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The reach is 90 m between manholes and the hose was marked every 10 m.
Hose marks at the reel show only 70 m paid out on the cleaning visit.
The camera audit finds debris untouched in the last 20 m.
The first 70 m is clean on the audit run.
No obstruction is found that would stop the hose at 70 m.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Debris in the last 20 m washed in after the cleaning
The hose marks were read incorrectly by the auditor
A hidden obstruction stopped the hose and the crew reported honestly
The cleaning stopped short of the full reach, leaving the last 20 m uncleaned

inference.explanation: Clean pipe exactly where the hose reached, untouched debris exactly where it did not, and no obstruction found make short cleaning the fit. Washed in debris would not respect the 70 m line so neatly.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best prevents short cleaning on future visits?

options.label: Crew self report form with no measurements
Annual camera audit of random reaches only
Cleaning log requiring hose payout length and a downstream manhole debris check for every reach

nextClue.explanation: A payout length plus a downstream check makes full reach cleaning verifiable on the day.

clueText.nc-a: A self report without measurements is what allowed this short cleaning to pass.
clueText.nc-b: Random audits catch some cases late, after debris has sat for months.
clueText.nc-c: The log records 90 m payout and debris captured at the far manhole for this reach on the recheck.

tasks.prompt: A pipe reported as collapsed on an old CCTV report in a prairie city turns out sound when it is cleaned and re inspected.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian inspection after cleaning. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The old report was made through heavy deposits with the camera half blinded.
After cleaning, the new camera run shows a round, sound pipe with no cracks.
The supposed collapse shadow in the old video matches the deposit pile shape.
Flow through the reach was never fully blocked, only slowed.
No surface depression ever formed above the reach.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The original inspection was made through deposits and misread a deposit pile as a collapse
The pipe collapsed and then returned to shape on its own
The cleaning process repaired the pipe wall
The new camera missed the collapse that the old one saw

inference.explanation: A sound pipe after cleaning, a deposit shaped shadow in the old video, and no surface depression fit a misread inspection. Buried pipe does not collapse and heal, and cleaning does not repair walls.

nextClue.prompt: Which practice best prevents this misread on future inspections?

options.label: Require cleaning before CCTV condition grading, with deposit levels noted when a run must be done dirty
Grade pipe condition from the first camera run regardless of deposits
Repeat the old report wording in the asset file

nextClue.explanation: Grading clean pipe, or flagging dirty runs, keeps deposits from being recorded as defects.

clueText.nc-a: The cleaned run grades the pipe sound, and the file now notes the first run was deposit blinded.
clueText.nc-b: Grading through deposits is exactly what produced the false collapse.
clueText.nc-c: Repeating old wording would carry the error into the asset record.

tasks.prompt: A town in British Columbia jets a wipes prone reach monthly, but a trial of quarterly jetting with a camera check shows no loss of service.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian cleaning interval trial. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Monthly jetting returns had been light for a year, mostly loose paper.
The trial reach is checked by camera at each quarterly visit and shows only light buildup.
No backups occur during the four quarter trial.
A second reach with known heavy root growth is kept on its short interval.
Crew hours saved are redeployed to the root reach.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Wipes stopped entering the reach during the trial year
The monthly interval was more frequent than this reach needs, and quarterly cleaning with checks holds service at lower cost
The camera checks themselves are cleaning the reach
Quarterly cleaning works for every reach in town

inference.explanation: Light returns, light camera findings, and no backups over a full trial year support a longer interval here, while the heavy root reach is deliberately kept short, so the finding is reach specific, not universal.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best justifies keeping the quarterly interval?

options.label: Crew hour savings total for the year
Trial log of camera findings, return volumes, and backup counts across the four quarters
A wipe disposal survey of the catchment

nextClue.explanation: Service evidence across the trial, not savings alone, justifies the interval change.

clueText.nc-a: Savings alone could hide a service loss, and the trial recorded none.
clueText.nc-b: The log shows light buildup and zero backups in all four quarters at the quarterly interval.
clueText.nc-c: A survey does not measure what actually built up in the pipe.

tasks.prompt: Jetting a long flat reach in a valley town clears the upstream half, but debris keeps reappearing at the downstream manhole for days.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian debris return after jetting. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The crew jetted without a vacuum truck at the downstream manhole.
Loosened debris settled in the flat reach instead of arriving at the manhole during jetting.
Each morning, flow works more settled debris down to the manhole.
When a vacuum truck is stationed downstream on the next cleaning, the reach stays clear.
Debris type is grit and rags, matching the reach deposits on CCTV.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: New debris is entering the reach every night from homes
The jetting nozzle is creating debris by breaking the pipe
Without capture at the downstream manhole, jetting loosened debris that resettled and kept migrating down
Downstream debris is a different material arriving from another reach

inference.explanation: Resettling in a flat reach, morning migration, matching material, and a clean result once vacuum capture is used fit uncaptured debris. Nightly home input would not match the deposit material so exactly.

nextClue.prompt: Which standing practice best closes this cleaning gap?

options.label: Jet the reach twice as often with no capture
Leave debris at the manhole for daily raking only
Pair jetting with vacuum capture at the downstream manhole on flat reaches, confirmed by a next day camera check

nextClue.explanation: Capture at the outlet plus a verification pass is what turns loosening into removal on flat reaches.

clueText.nc-a: More frequent jetting without capture repeats the loosen and resettle cycle.
clueText.nc-b: Daily raking treats the manhole symptom while debris keeps arriving from the reach.
clueText.nc-c: With vacuum capture and a clean next day camera, the reach stays clear for the season.
